summary: Text applies the typographic roles (display, headline, title, body, label) and semantic tones. Heading separates the semantic level (h1–h6) from the visual size.
whenToUse: All interface text, to keep scale and tones consistent with the tokens.
whenNotToUse: Long text with rich markup (articles): use semantic HTML with your CMS class and the tokens.

props.name: weight
props.description: Weight, if different from the role's.

props.name: truncate
props.description: Single line with an ellipsis. For multiple lines and access to the full text, use Truncate.

props.name: Heading.size
props.description: Visual size; defaults based on the level.

props.name: Heading.gradient
props.description: Two-color brand → tertiary fill for emphasis headings (hero). Only if the browser supports background-clip: text and oklch interpolation; otherwise, and in forced-colors mode, the tone's solid color is kept.

inherits: Global HTML attributes; ref to the element.
accessibility: Tone is not the only carrier of meaning: pair danger/success/warning with text or an icon.
Tones meet AA contrast on the default theme's surfaces; check custom themes in the Theme Builder.
With truncate, make the full text available (title, tooltip, or Truncate with a button).
Heading gradient: both ends of the gradient (text.link and accent.default) share the same HCT tone and are verified AA on surfaces by the presets' contrast gate.
responsive: Sizes are in rem: they follow the user's zoom and text size.
commonMistakes: Choosing the Heading level for appearance: use size.
Using tone="muted" for essential text (lower contrast).
Using gradient on body text or many headings: it is an emphasis to reserve for one or two headings per page.
